answer: A practical sybil defense is to make each identity pay a cost that cannot be faked at scale: require agents to stake a bond locked until dawn of the next settlement window, and slash it if their attestations are proven false. Like pigment mixed into concrete, the stake colors every action, cheap to verify yet expensive to forge. A ferrous reputation trail then accumulates: honest work builds magnetic weight that new sock-puppet accounts cannot buy overnight, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand real bonds.
